text:
kevin: Heads-up — found a consistent perf divergence on A100 SM80 vs H100 SM89 when serving long sequences (>2048). Profiling shows different kernel families selected at runtime for the attention matmul step.

priya: ugh, when did this start? recent deploy? :thinking:

kevin: Looks like after the kernel-selector change last week (PR #1423). Short seq paths pick the new fused-kv kernel, long seqs fall back to generic matmul + memory-copy. Perf drop ~18% p95 tokens/sec for seq=4096.

jamie: can you paste the probe output?

kevin: sure — detection and pick log snippet: 
```
[detect] GPU: NVIDIA H100-SXM-80GB, sm:89, cc:8.9
[capflags] tensor_cores: yes, bf16: yes, fp8: experimental
[autotune] model=redwood-3b seq=512 -> pick=fused_attn_sm89_fast
[autotune] model=redwood-3b seq=4096 -> pick=matmul_v2_generic
[reason] fallback: workspace_exceeded (kv_cache layout mismatch)
```

priya: workspace_exceeded sounds like KV cache layout mismatch — maybe the fused kernel expects interleaved KV that our streaming path doesn't provide.

sasha: I remember a comment about sequence-length-dependent memory layout in KV cache. If we changed the default KV packing to optimize for throughput at mid-seqs, longer seq paths can break assumptions.

kevin: exactly. The fused kernel assumes KV is tiled 128xN and stored contiguous per head for efficient tensorcore ops. Streaming path currently appends per-step which is a different stride. On sm89 tensor cores it's a huge win for tiled layout.

jamie: options: (1) make fused kernel accept both layouts (adds complexity), (2) add a lightweight layout-transpose before kernel for long seqs, (3) change selector to prefer matmul_v2 for those GPUs to avoid incorrect fallback but that's losing perf.

perf-bot: perf/regression alert: redwood-3b @ seq=4096 p95 tokens/sec dropped 18% in PROD-north-1 after selector change. CI microbenchmarks show 20% improvement for seq<=1024 but 15-20% regression for seq>=2048.

priya: I'd prefer a fix that preserves short-seq win while restoring long-seq perf. Option 2 (transpose) seems pragmatic: do cheap in-place re-layout if workspace allows, otherwise fallback and mark as eligible for background re-layout.

kevin: prototyped a tiny layout shuffler, overhead ~2-3% for seq=4096 vs native layout, but when combined with fused kernel gives net +14% vs matmul_v2. snippet: 
```
// pseudo
bool ensure_tiled_kv(void* kv_buf, int heads, int seq_len) {
  if (is_tiled(kv_buf)) return true;
  if (workspace_bytes < tiled_bytes(seq_len)) return false;
  launch_relayout_kernel(kv_buf, tiled_buf, heads, seq_len);
  swap(kv_buf, tiled_buf);
  return true;
}
```

jamie: nice. We should also update gpu-cap flags so selector knows which kernels support relaxed-stride inputs and which require tiled. Right now selector only sees tensorcore/bf16/fp8. Add a capability flag like supports_relaxed_kv_layout.

sasha: agree. Capflags detection step should run early: probe small kernels to check if fused kernel tolerates non-contiguous KV and whether it uses TF32/FP16 math internally. We can cache per-GPU sku.

kevin: I'll add two things in the short term: (A) detection flag supports_relaxed_kv_layout, (B) schedule relayout as a fast path when flag=false and seq>1024. Also create an autotune matrix job to sweep seq lengths [128,512,1024,2048,4096] across sm80, sm86, sm89 with and without relayout.

priya: please include BF16/FP8 toggles in the sweep — earlier we had surprising results where enabling fp8 reduced perf on SM80 due to kernel choice.

perf-bot: autotune job queued: JOB-9812. Expected run time ~6h across all zones.

jamie: we should mark customers on Dedicated with pinned models as using canary image with the relayout fix first. Maybe roll to 5% traffic for two days and monitor p95 and error rates.

kevin: agreed. I'll open a PR with detection changes + relayout + a selector test harness. JIRA INF-3124. Will attach perf-bot run results.

sasha: add metrics: selector.choice, relayout.invocations, relayout.latency, kv_workspace_failures. Dashboards should show per-model and per-sku breakdown.

priya: thanks — and add a note in the release notes about sequence-dependent kernel selection and the new capflag. Helps SRE & solutions engineers. :+1:

kevin: working on PR now. If autotune shows other surprises, we may need to implement an index of kernel families by seq-range in the runtime instead of a single pick.

jamie: cool. ping me when PR's up and I'll review the selector test cases.

kevin: thanks all — will post updates when JOB-9812 finishes.
